Join to apply for the Supply Chain Analyst role at Gastops.

Over the last 40 years, Gastops has built a robust business which is recognized worldwide for its innovative contributions to equipment health management in the aviation, energy, marine, industrial and transportation industries. Gastops' products and services add value throughout the life cycle of complex critical equipment from the design stage through to in-service operations and support. We design, manufacture, and support advanced equipment sensing and analysis products, including on-line oil debris sensors, torque measurement sensors, turbine blade health sensors, and at-line oil analysis systems.

As a Supply Chain Analyst at Gastops, you will play a key role in optimizing our supply chain operations through data-driven insights and ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) leadership. You will be responsible for analyzing procurement and logistics data, developing performance reports, and supporting cross-functional teams to enhance efficiency and decision-making across the supply chain. You will also serve as the functional lead for ERP-related supply chain processes, ensuring system integrity and continuous improvement.

What You'll Do

• Data Analysis & Reporting • Analyze supply chain data (inventory, procurement, lead times, supplier performance, etc.) to identify trends, variances, and areas for improvement.
• Develop and maintain dashboards and reports to track KPIs and support strategic decision-making.
• Collaborate with operations, finance, and engineering teams to gather requirements and provide data-driven insights.

• ERP System Leadership • Serve as the functional lead for ERP systems related to supply chain processes (e.g., procurement, inventory, BOMs, production planning).
• Maintain data integrity in ERP systems and lead initiatives to improve automation and data accuracy.
• Support ERP upgrades, configuration changes, and training for supply chain users.

• Process Improvement • Assist in the development and implementation of best practices for procurement, material planning, and inventory control.
• Work with stakeholders to identify inefficiencies and develop solutions to improve overall supply chain performance.

• Supplier & Inventory Management • Support supplier evaluation through performance metrics and risk analysis.
• Assist with inventory optimization strategies, including safety stock levels and reorder points.

• Operational Support • Support other supply chain functions, such as shipping, receiving, inventory control, material planning, and procurement, as needed.
• Assist in managing cycle counts, physical inventory, and reconciliation processes.

Who You Are:
• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, or a related field.
• 3+ years of experience in a supply chain or operations analysis role.
• Proficient with ERP systems (e.g., Epicor, SAP, Oracle, or equivalent).
• Strong analytical skills and advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel (pivot tables, lookups, charts, etc.).
• Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) is an asset.
• Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.
• Detail-oriented with strong problem-solving capabilities.
Preferred:
• Experience in a manufacturing or engineering-based environment, ideally in aerospace, defence, or energy sectors.
• Experience with Epicor Kinetic ERP system.
• Familiarity with ISO, AS9100, or other regulated environments.
• Understanding of Lean, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement.
What We Offer You:
• Competitive salary, benefits, profit share bonus program
• A fantastic culture, team, and energy to work with
• Superb work location in Ottawa (Canotek Business Park)
• Social activities, company-sponsored events and opportunities to give back to our local community
Gastops is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to acquiring a skilled and diverse workforce. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, origins, ages, orientations, genders, creeds and religions. job_title: Data Analyst Intern - SUMMER 2025 (3-months) at Electronic Arts Canada
job_description:
Data Analyst Intern - SUMMER 2025 (3-months) job at Electronic Arts. Canada.

We exist to Inspire the World to Play. We create extraordinary new game experiences for our millions of players everywhere by bringing together talented people that combine creativity, innovation, and passion. We immerse our employees into an inclusive culture and provide opportunities for learning and leading that allow our employees to do the most impactful and rewarding work of their careers.

Join us in driving the next revolution in games.

We’re looking for a Data Analyst Intern to join our world-class paid internship experience. The start date for this opportunity is May 2025 (3-month term).

You will report to the Senior Security Software Engineer II in the SPEAR (Secure Product Engineering & Anti-Cheat Response) Automation team, part of EA Security. You’ll be working closely with the SPEAR Automation team, helping to uncover and present actionable insights that will shape security strategies for our game studios and partner teams. Your work will provide critical support to EA’s CISO and other security stakeholders, turning raw data into meaningful information that enhances decision-making.
Responsibilities
• Analyse data generated from our source code security scanning platform and deliver insights to help game studios and the security team understand security trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
• Collaborate with the security team to produce dashboards, reports, and metrics that answer key security questions from senior leaders and other stakeholders.
• Identify patterns, trends, and anomalies within data sets that will drive actionable recommendations.
• Assist in the design and implementation of data models that improve how data is structured, stored, and utilised for reporting purposes.
• Partner with development and security teams to ensure data from different sources is gathered, cleansed, and analysed effectively.
Requirements
• Pursuing a degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field.
• Proficiency with data analysis tools and languages, such as SQL, Python, R, or equivalent.
• Strong understanding of statistical analysis and data visualisation techniques.
• Familiarity with security concepts or a willingness to quickly learn about the world of source code security and vulnerability scanning.
• Strong communication skills with the ability to translate data insights into clear, actionable recommendations.
• We are only considering students mid-way through their college career, slated to graduate no earlier than December 2025. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the US on a full time basis during the 12-week internship. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
Desirable
• Experience with business intelligence tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI).
• Familiarity with working with large data sets and cleaning/manipulating data.
• Understanding of API usage and integration for data extraction.
• Interest in cyber security and the tech industry.

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

Growth & Commercial Analyst (Grid Services)

The Company

Powerhouse Generation (PHG) is a leading energy management and Demand Side Unit (DSU) aggregator operating across the all-island electricity market. We act as a virtual power station, connecting large commercial, industrial, and institutional energy users, such as manufacturing plants, hospitals, and commercial facilities, directly to the power grid. By optimising real-time electricity demand and enabling remote grid balancing, we empower our clients to unlock new revenue streams, reduce carbon impacts, and contribute to a more stable, sustainable energy grid.

Strategic Context

Powerhouse Generation’s growth agenda includes converting the iSEM sales pipeline into contracted MW capacity for the 2027/28 capacity year, expanding existing customer relationships, progressing new industrial and energy-intense customers, and building a repeatable pipeline for subsequent years. The role must keep near-term contract conversion on track while supporting longer-term growth opportunities. The individual is not simply responsible for producing reports: they are expected to drive actions and help opportunities progress.

The Role

This is a high-impact role for an ambitious commercial analyst or business development professional who wants broad exposure to strategy, customers, energy markets and executive decision-making. Success means the CGO has better information, more time with strategic customers, fewer stalled actions and a materially higher probability of delivering PHG’s contracted MW and growth objectives.

The Purpose To act as the Chief Growth Officer’s commercial wingman, turning PHG’s growth strategy into a controlled programme of customer acquisition, contracted capacity, revenue and EBITDA growth. The role combines commercial analysis, account and pipeline management, project coordination and executive-level reporting. It is designed to increase the CGO’s capacity to win and expand strategic accounts by ensuring that opportunities are properly analysed, actions are followed through, internal blockers are surfaced early, and decisions are supported by reliable data.

Key responsibilities

• Growth plan and execution

Translate the CGO’s growth priorities into a practical action plan with milestones, owners, dependencies and decision dates.

Maintain a clear view of contracted MW, forecast MW, probability-weighted pipeline, revenue and EBITDA implications where data is available.

Track progress against monthly targets and identify slippage, gaps and corrective actions early.

Coordinate cross-functional actions required to move opportunities from initial discussion through proposal, heads of terms, contract and readiness for registration/qualification.

Prepare concise decision papers and recommendations for the CGO and executive team.

• Commercial pipeline and account management

Own the accuracy and discipline of the growth pipeline, including stage, validated MW, customer sponsor, next action, close date, capacity year and probability.

Prepare for and coordinate weekly pipeline reviews; record decisions, owners and deadlines, and chase actions through to completion.

Develop account plans for priority customers and support the CGO with customer research, stakeholder maps, meeting briefs and follow-up notes.

Support multi-site and group-level commercial propositions, standardised site schedules, proposals, term sheets and framework agreements.

Identify stalled deals, understand the blocker, coordinate a recovery plan and recommend when an opportunity should be re-scoped, re-priced, re-timed or closed.

Support early-stage qualification of prospects by collecting site data, validating potential MW and coordinating technical/commercial assessment.

• Market, data and commercial analysis

Analyse customer sites, flexibility potential, operating profiles, available capacity and relevant market routes in coordination with PHG’s technical and markets specialists.

Build and maintain commercial models, opportunity comparisons and sensitivities covering MW, revenue, costs, margin and EBITDA where inputs are available.

Research target sectors and accounts, including industrial and energy-intense customers, data centres, battery energy storage and other relevant flexibility assets.

Track relevant market developments, customer investment plans and regulatory/market changes that may affect PHG’s proposition; flag implications rather than provide unsupported conclusions.

Challenge assumptions and data quality, distinguish verified facts from estimates, and make uncertainty visible in forecasts.

• Contracting and delivery coordination

Coordinate the commercial workflow from proposal to signed agreement, working with legal, finance, technical and delivery colleagues.

Maintain a live list of contract, funding, technical, metering, registration and qualification dependencies for priority sites.

Ensure site capacity, expected availability date and capacity-year assumptions are reconciled before an opportunity is counted as deliverable.

Support preparation of customer and internal approval packs and keep a record of decisions and outstanding conditions.

Escalate risks that could prevent a site from meeting the relevant qualification or go-live deadline.

• Executive support and operating rhythm

Prepare a short weekly growth dashboard and monthly executive scorecard.

Create concise customer meeting briefs, presentation materials, board/executive updates and follow-up action logs.

Maintain a single source of truth for pipeline data until a CRM or other system is implemented.

Organise growth review meetings and ensure the CGO’s time is focused on the decisions, relationships and negotiations with the greatest impact.

Handle commercially sensitive information with discretion and maintain high standards of accuracy and confidentiality.

WhatWe’reLookingFor

Essential

Strong analytical and commercial skills, with confidence working with data, forecasts and business cases.

Excellent Excel skills; able to build and maintain structured models, dashboards and trackers. PowerPoint proficiency is also required.

Strong project coordination and follow-through: able to manage multiple opportunities, deadlines, dependencies and stakeholders.

Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to turn complex information into concise executive summaries.

Commercial judgement, curiosity and confidence to question assumptions, identify gaps and escalate risks constructively.

Highly organised, proactive and comfortable working in a fast-moving environment with changing priorities.

Discretion when handling customer, contract, pricing and company information.

Willingness to learn the Irish and Northern Irish energy markets, flexibility services and relevant capacity/qualification processes.

Must have a full driver’s licence and own travel.

Desirable

Experience in energy, utilities, demand response, energy aggregation, flexibility, generation, BESS or industrial energy management.

Experience supporting business development, key accounts, commercial contracts or strategic growth programmes.

Familiarity with financial modelling, revenue/margin analysis, CRM tools and pipeline forecasting.

Experience coordinating technical, commercial, legal and operational teams.

Relevant degree or equivalent experience in business, finance, economics, engineering, energy or data analytics.

Personal attributes A self-starter who anticipates what the CGO will need next.

Commercially assertive without overstepping decision authority.

Comfortable engaging with customers and senior internal stakeholders.

Practical and delivery-oriented: values signed contracts and completed actions over activity for its own sake.

Able to work independently, maintain attention to detail and keep momentum across a broad portfolio.

Location

Ireland / Northern Ireland, with travel to customer sites as required

Employee Share Options Scheme

Private medical insurance

Company pension

Company social events

Gym on site

Parking on site

Additional days leave

Bike to work scheme

Devices: Company phone and laptop

Growth & Commercial Analyst (Grid Services)

The Company

Powerhouse Generation (PHG) is a leading energy management and Demand Side Unit (DSU) aggregator operating across the all-island electricity market. We act as a virtual power station, connecting large commercial, industrial, and institutional energy users, such as manufacturing plants, hospitals, and commercial facilities, directly to the power grid. By optimising real-time electricity demand and enabling remote grid balancing, we empower our clients to unlock new revenue streams, reduce carbon impacts, and contribute to a more stable, sustainable energy grid.

Strategic Context

Powerhouse Generation’s growth agenda includes converting the iSEM sales pipeline into contracted MW capacity for the 2027/28 capacity year, expanding existing customer relationships, progressing new industrial and energy-intense customers, and building a repeatable pipeline for subsequent years. The role must keep near-term contract conversion on track while supporting longer-term growth opportunities. The individual is not simply responsible for producing reports: they are expected to drive actions and help opportunities progress.

The Role

This is a high-impact role for an ambitious commercial analyst or business development professional who wants broad exposure to strategy, customers, energy markets and executive decision-making. Success means the CGO has better information, more time with strategic customers, fewer stalled actions and a materially higher probability of delivering PHG’s contracted MW and growth objectives.

The Purpose To act as the Chief Growth Officer’s commercial wingman, turning PHG’s growth strategy into a controlled programme of customer acquisition, contracted capacity, revenue and EBITDA growth. The role combines commercial analysis, account and pipeline management, project coordination and executive-level reporting. It is designed to increase the CGO’s capacity to win and expand strategic accounts by ensuring that opportunities are properly analysed, actions are followed through, internal blockers are surfaced early, and decisions are supported by reliable data.

Key responsibilities

• Growth plan and execution

Translate the CGO’s growth priorities into a practical action plan with milestones, owners, dependencies and decision dates.

Maintain a clear view of contracted MW, forecast MW, probability-weighted pipeline, revenue and EBITDA implications where data is available.

Track progress against monthly targets and identify slippage, gaps and corrective actions early.

Coordinate cross-functional actions required to move opportunities from initial discussion through proposal, heads of terms, contract and readiness for registration/qualification.

Prepare concise decision papers and recommendations for the CGO and executive team.

• Commercial pipeline and account management

Own the accuracy and discipline of the growth pipeline, including stage, validated MW, customer sponsor, next action, close date, capacity year and probability.

Prepare for and coordinate weekly pipeline reviews; record decisions, owners and deadlines, and chase actions through to completion.

Develop account plans for priority customers and support the CGO with customer research, stakeholder maps, meeting briefs and follow-up notes.

Support multi-site and group-level commercial propositions, standardised site schedules, proposals, term sheets and framework agreements.

Identify stalled deals, understand the blocker, coordinate a recovery plan and recommend when an opportunity should be re-scoped, re-priced, re-timed or closed.

Support early-stage qualification of prospects by collecting site data, validating potential MW and coordinating technical/commercial assessment.

• Market, data and commercial analysis

Analyse customer sites, flexibility potential, operating profiles, available capacity and relevant market routes in coordination with PHG’s technical and markets specialists.

Build and maintain commercial models, opportunity comparisons and sensitivities covering MW, revenue, costs, margin and EBITDA where inputs are available.

Research target sectors and accounts, including industrial and energy-intense customers, data centres, battery energy storage and other relevant flexibility assets.

Track relevant market developments, customer investment plans and regulatory/market changes that may affect PHG’s proposition; flag implications rather than provide unsupported conclusions.

Challenge assumptions and data quality, distinguish verified facts from estimates, and make uncertainty visible in forecasts.

• Contracting and delivery coordination

Coordinate the commercial workflow from proposal to signed agreement, working with legal, finance, technical and delivery colleagues.

Maintain a live list of contract, funding, technical, metering, registration and qualification dependencies for priority sites.

Ensure site capacity, expected availability date and capacity-year assumptions are reconciled before an opportunity is counted as deliverable.

Support preparation of customer and internal approval packs and keep a record of decisions and outstanding conditions.

Escalate risks that could prevent a site from meeting the relevant qualification or go-live deadline.

• Executive support and operating rhythm

Prepare a short weekly growth dashboard and monthly executive scorecard.

Create concise customer meeting briefs, presentation materials, board/executive updates and follow-up action logs.

Maintain a single source of truth for pipeline data until a CRM or other system is implemented.

Organise growth review meetings and ensure the CGO’s time is focused on the decisions, relationships and negotiations with the greatest impact.

Handle commercially sensitive information with discretion and maintain high standards of accuracy and confidentiality.

WhatWe’reLookingFor

Essential

Strong analytical and commercial skills, with confidence working with data, forecasts and business cases.

Excellent Excel skills; able to build and maintain structured models, dashboards and trackers. PowerPoint proficiency is also required.

Strong project coordination and follow-through: able to manage multiple opportunities, deadlines, dependencies and stakeholders.

Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to turn complex information into concise executive summaries.

Commercial judgement, curiosity and confidence to question assumptions, identify gaps and escalate risks constructively.

Highly organised, proactive and comfortable working in a fast-moving environment with changing priorities.

Discretion when handling customer, contract, pricing and company information.

Willingness to learn the Irish and Northern Irish energy markets, flexibility services and relevant capacity/qualification processes.

Must have a full driver’s licence and own travel.

Desirable

Experience in energy, utilities, demand response, energy aggregation, flexibility, generation, BESS or industrial energy management.

Experience supporting business development, key accounts, commercial contracts or strategic growth programmes.

Familiarity with financial modelling, revenue/margin analysis, CRM tools and pipeline forecasting.

Experience coordinating technical, commercial, legal and operational teams.

Relevant degree or equivalent experience in business, finance, economics, engineering, energy or data analytics.

Personal attributes A self-starter who anticipates what the CGO will need next.

Commercially assertive without overstepping decision authority.

Comfortable engaging with customers and senior internal stakeholders.

Practical and delivery-oriented: values signed contracts and completed actions over activity for its own sake.

Able to work independently, maintain attention to detail and keep momentum across a broad portfolio.

Location

Ireland / Northern Ireland, with travel to customer sites as required

• Assist with inventory optimization strategies, including safety stock levels and reorder points.

• Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.
• Detail-oriented with strong problem-solving capabilities.

• Experience with Epicor Kinetic ERP system.
• Familiarity with ISO, AS9100, or other regulated environments.
• Understanding of Lean, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement.

• Residency in Canada for the last 5 consecutive years

• Comfort with rigorous guideline interpretation and consistent framework application
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience in analytical, technical, or research disciplines (strongly preferred)
• Stable internet connection and access to a personal computer

Find Your Spot at Humber

At Humber, we are a vibrant, diverse community of professionals dedicated to providing an exceptional learning experience for our students. Through our strategic vision and exciting new brand Builders of Brilliance, we are co-constructing a new model of polytechnic education for Ontario, Canada, and the world. We are committed to ensuring that Humber offers the right programs and the most effective teaching and learning approaches to prepare exceptional leaders for our industries and communities.

To achieve our vision, we take finding and developing the right talent very seriously. We offer a collegial, collaborative, inclusive environment in which each individual is supported in growing and bringing their best each day.

If you are excited by the prospect of contributing to our vision for learning, if you would like to be part of building a new model of polytechnic education, of ‘building brilliance’, in one of Canada’s preeminent higher education institutions, then here is your opportunity to join our dynamic team.

Job Details:

Position Title: Business Analyst

Status: Full-Time Administration Contract

Hours: 37.5 hours per week

Faculty/Department: Information Technology Services

Campus/Location: North Campus – must be comfortable working hybrid, a minimum of four (4) days on-site.

Minimum Starting Salary: $97,491; starting salaries are determined based on qualifications and years of related experience.

Duration of Need: Until March 31, 2027

About the Information Technology Services at Humber:

Information Technology Services provides leadership for the continuous development of digital experiences delivered on a secure, flexible, and dependable IT environment built on a foundation of transparency, collaboration, client focus, and respect. Together we transform client ideas into results, leverage technology to enable student engagement and success, support students and employees in the journey of discovery, deliver integrated digital solutions to improve collaboration and communication across the Humber community, and improve business processes to enable better decision-making.

Digital

Innovation, Information Technology Services is always striving to enhance the digital experience for students, staff, and visitors.

About the Business Analyst Role:

The Business Analyst is responsible for supporting the discovery, analysis, planning, and delivery of strategic digital initiatives across Humber.

You will collaborate with business and technology interested parties to understand business needs, define problems and opportunities, document current and future-state processes, identify requirements, and support the evaluation of potential solutions.

Acting as a bridge between business needs and technology delivery, you will facilitate conversations with interested parties, translate business needs into clear and actionable requirements, and work collaboratively with Product Owners, Enterprise Architecture, technical teams, and business partners to support informed decision-making and successful delivery.

You will contribute throughout the initiative lifecycle, from early discovery and planning through requirements definition and implementation support, ensuring business objectives, requirements, decisions, dependencies, and expected outcomes are clearly understood and documented.

Ultimately, you are accountable for providing strong business analysis capability that enables Humber to better understand complex business problems, evaluate opportunities, and progress strategic initiatives toward measurable outcomes.

Key Duties

• Collaborating with business and technology interested parties to understand strategic objectives, business needs, challenges, and opportunities.
• Lead and support discovery activities, including interviews, workshops, process analysis, and requirements gathering.
• Analyze and document current-state and future-state business processes, identifying opportunities for improvement, simplification, and automation.
• Support Product Owners in defining, refining, and maintaining initiative backlogs and connecting detailed requirements to expected business outcomes.
• Partner with Enterprise Architecture and technical teams to provide the business context and requirements needed to evaluate solution options and inform recommendations.
• Facilitate cross-functional discussions to clarify requirements, resolve gaps, identify dependencies, and support alignment and decision-making.
• Support vendor and solution evaluation activities by documenting requirements, analyzing proposed capabilities, and assessing alignment with business needs.
• Support initiatives through planning and implementation by maintaining requirements traceability and helping ensure delivered solutions align with agreed business needs.
• Develop clear documentation and recommendations that enable leadership to make informed decisions.
• Contribute to the continuous improvement of Planning and Scoping practices, business analysis standards, templates, and ways of working across Humber.
Qualifications
About You:
You are passionate about working at Ontario's largest Polytechnic; you thrive on improving productivity and quality that contribute to team success! If this sounds like you, keep reading:

Education A Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Analysis, or a related field.

Experience/Skills

• Working knowledge of AI-assisted business analysis tools and techniques (e.g., prompt and context engineering, AI-assisted documentation and requirements drafting), with sound judgment to validate AI-generated outputs before they inform a decision

• Comfort operating in an evolving practice where AI increasingly supports requirements elicitation and documentation — while accountability for accuracy, business intent, and outcomes remains with the analyst

• Experience with Salesforce, AWS, and/or higher education systems and integrations is considered an asset

• Working knowledge of QA test planning, test execution, and coordination of user acceptance sign-off is considered an asset
• A minimum of five years of experience in business analysis, strategic analysis, digital transformation, or related roles within complex enterprise environments.

• Demonstrated experience leading discovery, requirements gathering, business process analysis, and future-state definition.

• Experience supporting complex digital or technology-enabled initiatives involving multiple business and technical interested parties.

• Strong facilitation and engagement skills, with the ability to lead discussions, workshops, and requirements sessions with diverse audiences.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess complex problems, identify opportunities, and develop practical recommendations.

• Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex information clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with Product Owners, Enterprise Architecture, technical teams, vendors, and business.

• Experience working within product, or iterative delivery environments and developing or managing work through structured backlogs.

• Experience with Azure DevOps or comparable work management tools is considered an asset.

• Experience supporting vendor evaluation, procurement, system implementation, or digital transformation initiatives is considered an asset.

• Experience within higher education or another complex public-sector environment is considered an asset.

If this sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you! At Humber Polytechnic we don't just accept difference we celebrate it! Experience comes in many forms, skills are transferable, and a progressive mindset goes a long way at Humber. If your experience is close to what we're looking for, consider applying and tell us why you are a great candidate for this job. Find your Spot at Humber!

What's in it for you?

• An opportunity to be a part of building Humber's future.
• Be part of a diverse, hard-working, and supportive team.
• Tools and technology that will allow you to succeed at your job.
• Amazing perks!
We thank you for your interest in working with Humber Polytechnic. Only applicants selected for an interview will be contacted.

Humber Polytechnic is committed to a workforce that reflects the diversity of our students and our city. Humber supports employment equity. Racialized workers, women, Indigenous workers, LGBTQ2S workers and workers with disabilities are encouraged to apply. job_description:
Junior Data Scientists, Quantitative Analysts & Machine Learning Researchers. Remote AI Project

We are seeking experienced Data Scientists, Quantitative Analysts, Machine Learning Researchers, and Statistical Modeling Professionals to contribute to a remote AI project focused on statistics, machine learning, experimentation, and quantitative reasoning.

You will evaluate AI-generated solutions to technical and quantitative problems, identify flawed methodology, create challenging prompts and datasets, develop reference solutions, and provide structured feedback that improves model performance.

What You’ll Do

• Evaluate AI-generated responses across data science, statistics, machine learning, experimentation, and quantitative analysis.
• Identify incorrect assumptions, statistical errors, flawed methodology, weak experimental design, and unsupported conclusions.
• Create challenging expert-level prompts based on realistic analytical and quantitative problems.
• Build or review datasets used to evaluate model performance.
• Develop reference solutions that demonstrate correct methodology and reasoning.
• Assess whether analytical approaches are statistically sound, reproducible, and appropriate for the problem.
• Review model reasoning related to experimentation, causal inference, forecasting, predictive modeling, and data interpretation.
• Evaluate code and analytical workflows when relevant.
• Provide structured technical feedback explaining why an approach is correct or incorrect.
• Help refine evaluation criteria and improve the difficulty and quality of quantitative tasks.

Who Can Apply

Relevant backgrounds include Data Scientists, Senior Data Analysts, Junior Data Scientists, Associate Data Scientists, Quantitative Analysts, Quantitative Researchers, and Applied Scientists.
We also welcome Machine Learning Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, Research Scientists, and Applied Machine Learning Researchers with strong quantitative foundations.

Statistics backgrounds may include Statisticians, Applied Statisticians, Biostatisticians, Statistical Analysts, and Statistical Modeling Specialists.

Experimentation backgrounds may include Experimentation Scientists, Product Data Scientists, Decision Scientists, Causal Inference Specialists, and A/B Testing Experts.

Finance backgrounds may include Quantitative Researchers, Quantitative Strategists, Financial Data Scientists, Risk Modelers, and Quantitative Finance Professionals.

Additional relevant backgrounds include Econometricians, Operations Research Scientists, Analytics Scientists, Research Analysts, and Computational Researchers with strong statistical expertise.

Requirements

• At least one year of professional experience in data science, quantitative analysis, statistics, machine learning, finance, research, or a closely related field.
• At least part of that experience must have occurred within the past three years.
• Strong foundation in statistics, probability, and quantitative reasoning.
• Experience analyzing real-world datasets and interpreting results.
• Ability to identify flawed methodology and statistical errors.
• Strong understanding of experimentation or model evaluation principles.
• Working knowledge of Python, R, SQL, or comparable quantitative tools.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to communicate technical and statistical concepts clearly in writing.
• Comfortable working independently in a remote environment.

Preferred Background

• Professional experience at a leading technology company, financial institution, research organization, or quantitatively rigorous company.
• Experience in product data science, experimentation, quantitative research, applied machine learning, statistics, or analytics.
• Experience designing or reviewing A/B tests, predictive models, or quantitative research.
• Experience with causal inference, forecasting, recommendation systems, risk modeling, or optimization is valuable.
• Experience reviewing technical analyses, research reports, or model outputs for methodological quality.
• Experience creating technical assessments, analytical case studies, interview problems, or quantitative benchmarks is helpful.

This opportunity is ideal for quantitative professionals who can look at a statistical or machine learning problem, identify whether the methodology is genuinely sound, catch subtle errors in assumptions or evaluation, build a rigorous reference solution, and clearly explain why one analytical approach is stronger than another. CMPA's AI & Advanced Analytics team builds AI solutions that process sensitive medical-legal content. We are looking for a co-op student to focus on transforming raw medical-legal data into AI-ready datasets: cleaned, standardized, labeled, and governed so they can reliably train, fine-tune, and evaluate AI models. This role works entirely with internally hosted data and infrastructure (on-prem GPU servers) to maintain strict privacy and security for PHI/PII, and supports real production pipelines already in active development.

Develop Python scripts and lightweight data pipelines for ingesting, de‑identifying, chunking, formatting, and validating documents at scale, with traceability suitable for audit review. Create and maintain evaluation/test sets (e.g., scripted advisor-member conversation samples) to benchmark transcription, summarization, and classification performance. Document data preparation standards, labeling guidelines, and known data quality issues so the process is repeatable, governed, and auditable across teams. Work closely with the AI program lead to align data preparation work with governance, privacy, and security requirements for regulated healthcare data. Support document classification and medical‑legal coding workflows by preparing labeled datasets and validating tagging accuracy against existing coding schemes. EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE Currently enrolled in a co‑op program in Computer Science, Data Science, Health Informatics, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Foundational Python programming skills, including experience working with structured or unstructured data. Experience with libraries such as pandas, regular expressions, spaCy, or similar is an asset. Familiarity with core NLP or document‑processing concepts—such as text normalization, tokenization, named‑entity recognition, classification, or information extraction—through coursework, personal projects, research, or prior work. Ability to work methodically with ambiguous, incomplete, and messy real‑world data. SKILLS AND ABILITIES Strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and comfort handling sensitive or high‑stakes information in accordance with established procedures. Ability to document data transformations, assumptions, validation steps, and known limitations clearly and consistently. Strong written communication and an ability to collaborate remotely with technical and non‑technical stakeholders. Exposure to healthcare, legal, insurance, public‑sector, or other regulated‑domain data is an asset. Familiarity with privacy‑preserving data practices, including de‑identification or anonymization of PHI/PII is an asset. Exposure to data quality, data lineage, metadata, data governance, audit, privacy, security, or compliance concepts is an asset. Exposure to speech‑to‑text, document OCR, document parsing, or text‑extraction pipelines is an asset. This is not a one-time data-cleanup role: the student will help establish reusable data foundations that support CMPA’s broader AI roadmap. This placement offers a rare opportunity to see how disciplined data engineering—including data quality, traceability, privacy protection, and documentation—affects the reliability and auditability of AI systems in a regulated, high-stakes environment.
POSITION OVERVIEW

CMPA's AI & Advanced Analytics team builds AI solutions that process sensitive medical-legal content. We are looking for a co-op student to focus on transforming raw medical-legal data into AI-ready datasets: cleaned, standardized, labeled, and governed so they can reliably train, fine-tune, and evaluate AI models. This role works entirely with internally hosted data and infrastructure (on-prem GPU servers) to maintain strict privacy and security for PHI/PII, and supports real production pipelines already in active development.

You will gain hands‑on experience designing data pipelines and quality controls for sensitive, unstructured information; applying privacy and governance principles in practice; and contributing to AI capabilities that are being developed for real organizational use. You will work closely with experienced AI, data, privacy, and domain professionals.

Help define and apply AI-readiness criteria for medical-legal datasets — completeness, consistency, labeling accuracy, lineage, and auditability — so data quality becomes measurable rather than assumed. Develop Python scripts and lightweight data pipelines for ingesting, de‑identifying, chunking, formatting, and validating documents at scale, with traceability suitable for audit review. Create and maintain evaluation/test sets (e.g., scripted advisor-member conversation samples) to benchmark transcription, summarization, and classification performance. Document data preparation standards, labeling guidelines, and known data quality issues so the process is repeatable, governed, and auditable across teams. Work closely with the AI program lead to align data preparation work with governance, privacy, and security requirements for regulated healthcare data. Support document classification and medical‑legal coding workflows by preparing labeled datasets and validating tagging accuracy against existing coding schemes. EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE Currently enrolled in a co‑op program in Computer Science, Data Science, Health Informatics, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Foundational Python programming skills, including experience working with structured or unstructured data. Familiarity with core NLP or document‑processing concepts—such as text normalization, tokenization, named‑entity recognition, classification, or information extraction—through coursework, personal projects, research, or prior work. job_description:
Rockwell Automation is a global technology leader focused on helping the world's manufacturers be more productive, sustainable, and agile. With more than 28,000 employees who make the world better every day, we know we have something special. Behind our customers - amazing companies that help feed the world, provide life-saving medicine on a global scale, and focus on clean water and green mobility - our people are energized problem solvers that take pride in how the work we do changes the world for the better.

We welcome all makers, forward thinkers, and problem solvers who are looking for a place to do their best work. And if that's you we would love to have you join us!
Job Description

The Robotics Research Co-op is part of the Robotics Centre of Excellence (RCoE). The RCoE is the "innovation engine" of Rockwell Automation robotics. We are a dynamic, research group dedicated pre-programmed automation and ushering in the new era of Autonomous Operations. Here, you'll work with world-class experts in a culture that prizes rapid prototyping and the desire to see "impossible" ideas working on the factory floor.

We are looking for a passionate Robotics Research Intern who is at the intersection of AI theory and hands-on implementation. You will work with senior researchers, gaining invaluable hands-on experience with modern embodied intelligence. Your work will centre on building data tooling and pipelines. These pipelines move, curate, and integrate data into our platform. They directly help develop perception and world models. We achieve this support through the use of machine learning frameworks.

Relocation assistance is not available or provided for this role.
Your Responsibilities
• Build data tooling and pipelines to integrate robot and perception data into our platform. These pipelines support dataset curation and ensure model evaluation workflows, including dataset slicing and active learning loops for continuous improvement.
• Collect robot and perception datasets using LiDAR, cameras, and other sensors across a range of scenarios, including both structured experiments and real-world deployments.
• Organise perception datasets, contributing to the creation of high-quality datasets for model training and evaluation.
• Write clean, scalable, and code applying modern system programming languages and following software engineering best practices.
• Document your best practices and research through technical reports, white papers, and publications.
The Essentials – You Will Have
• Actively pursuing a bachelors or advanced degree at an accredited college or university.
• Legal authorization to work in Canada is required. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future for this job opening.
The Preferred – You Might Also Have
• Demonstrated experience working with datasets, including data processing, organisation, and curation to support machine learning workflows, with familiarity with common data quality issues and their mitigation.
• Experience with Machine Learning concepts, vision and applied robotics contexts, with a focus on how data impacts model performance.
• Hands-on experience working with robotics hardware and sensors.
• Foundation in software development, with the ability to design clean, maintainable systems and quickly understand unfamiliar codebases.
• Practical experience with PyTorch, Tensorflow, TensorRT, HuggingFace.
• Exposure to simulation environments or synthetic data generation workflows.
• Experience with ROS/ROS2
• Experience with robotics principles including state estimation and 3D processing
• Exposure to foundation models such as Vision-Language-Models
• Experience with cloud storage such as Azure, AWS, etc.
• Experience with containerization tools such as Docker, Apptainer.
• Experience with research, parsing academic publications, and literature review.

• Health Care Spending Account (HCSA - dependent on the plan chosen)
• Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

• Volunteering Time off

• Employer Paid DC Pension
• Maternity and Parental Leave Top-Up
• Fitness Reimbursement Program
• Flexible Work Schedule where you will work with your manager to enjoy a work schedule that can be flexible with your personal life.

This position is part of a job family. Experience will be the determining factor for position level and compensation.

For this role, the compensation is from $20 - $32 hourly. Actual pay will be based on factors such as skills, knowledge, education, and experience.

Magnet Forensics is a global leader in the development of digital investigative software that acquires, analyzes, and shares evidence from computers, smartphones, tablets, and IoT-related devices. At Magnet Forensics, you will be fully integrated into our software development team. You'll start by getting comfortable with the code, working through bugs and basic features, all the while writing code that will actually be seen in production. As you ramp, you’ll be given more complex features just like any other member of the team. In fact, some of the key features of our software were written by our students!

• You are a student working towards a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering or a related discipline
• You’re strong at object-oriented programming (Languages: Java/JavaScript, C#, C++, Python)

• You like working in a collaborative environment with smart, funny and interesting people

We hire passionate people who enjoy technical challenges. We love problem solvers who want to keep learning, individually and as part of the team. We want people who collaborate and help others. We foster a team environment where everyone is comfortable sharing their ideas, because we understand that with diversity of thought, we will build the best products.
Compensation & Benefits

At Magnet Forensics, we are committed to fair and consistent pay practices for our student roles.Hourly pay isdeterminedusing standardized, non-negotiable salary bands based on academic progression and the number of official completed work terms recognized by your academic institution.

$23.33 - $35.18 (Currency i.e. “CDN”) per hour

Salary Range (min - max)

Position Type: Current Vacancy
Indicators of Success

We’re looking for someone who checks off most, but not all, of the boxes listed in “skills and experiences”. It’s more important to us to find candidates who can display indicators of success through skills they have developed and experiences they have been a part of, than to find folks who have “been there, done that”. We want to be part of your development journey, and we’ll learn as much from you as you learn from us.
How We Work

At Magnet Forensics, we take a hybrid-flexible approach to support your productivity and work-life balance. If you’re within a comfortable travel distance to one of our offices, you’ll occasionally join us in person. How often you’ll come in depends on your department and team needs, typically ranging from weekly to monthly. These in-person moments help us build stronger connections, spark new ideas, and celebrate our successes together. Most days, you can choose what works best for you, while staying in tune with your team’s goals.

We’re excited to welcome you to our team and look forward to achieving great things together - both in the office and wherever you work best!
The Most Important Thing

We’re looking for candidates that can provide examples of how they have demonstrated Magnet CODE in their previous experiences:

CARE – We care about each other and our mission to make a difference in the world.

OWN – We are accountable for our results – while never forgetting to act with integrity, empathy, and respect.

job_description:
About Hivery

HIVERY, officially formed in 2015, began with an advanced AI system built with bleeding edge technologies from machine learning, operations research, and design discipline. This system remains at the core of HIVERY to this day, and is continuously improved by an ever-expanding team of scientists, engineers, and designers as we pursue and develop our ultimate vision: The Retail Genome®.

We are a venture backed startup and closed series B funding in July 2022. HIVERY Curate, our flagship product, is the world’s only store-level assortment and space strategy simulation and optimization solution. HIVERY Curate enables a retailer or category manager to run assortment and category simulations and understand the financial impact of any assortment and space decision. Originally located in Sydney, Australia HIVERY is now a globally distributed organization hiring for remote roles in engineering.

We are seeking a new or recent graduate to join us as a Data Engineer in our Curate engineering team. In this role you will:

• Develop features and improvements to the HIVERY Curate product in a secure, well-tested, and performant way.

• Collaborate with Product and other stakeholders within Engineering to maintain a high bar for quality in a fast-paced, iterative environment.

• Solve technical problems of low to moderate scope and complexity.

• Write code that meets our internal standards for style, maintainability, and best practices for data engineering in a high scale environment. Maintain and advocate for these standards through code review

• Collaborate to identify impediments to our efficiency as a team ("technical debt"), propose and implement solutions.

• Represent HIVERY and its values in public communication around specific projects and community contributions.

• Ship small features and improvements with guidance and support from senior team members.

• Participate on-call rotations

To be successful in this role you will need to have:

• Familiarity with object-oriented design patterns, data structures, and algorithms

• Professional or academic experience with Python or Go.

• Professional or academic experience with one or more cloud providers (Azure, AWS, GCP) and infrastructure as code.

• Professional or academic experience with data warehousing, ELT, or ELT

• Professional or academic experience with big data technologies such as Apache Hadoop, Spark, Iceberg

• Proficiency in the English language, both written and verbal, sufficient for success in a remote and asynchronous work environment.

• Excellent communication skills and a capability to communicate with both technical and nontechnical audiences.

• Experience with performance and optimization problems and a demonstrated ability to both diagnose and prevent these problems.

• Comfort working in a highly agile, intensely iterative software development process.

• Positive and solution-oriented mindset.

• Effective communication skills: Tactfully achieve consensus with peers, and clear status updates.

• An inclination towards communication, inclusion, and visibility.

• Self-motivated and self-managing, with excellent organizational skills.

• Share our values, and work in accordance with those values.

• Ability to thrive in a fully remote organization.

The pay range for this role is:

70,000 - 80,000 CAD per year(Remote - Canada)

You'll receive hands‑on mentorship and grow your skills on real enterprise projects.

Data Engineering (60%)
• Build and maintain ELT pipelines using Azure Data Factory, Databricks, or Fabric
• Write SQL queries for data transformations and validation
• Develop Python or Scala scripts for data processing
• Implement data quality checks and error handling
• Assist with data modeling (dimension and fact tables)

• Monitor pipeline executions and troubleshoot failures
Client Support (20%)

Nice to Have
